newsitem.title: FRANCE: More French watch TV daily in Q1 1997 - Mediametrie.
newsitem.headline: More French watch TV daily in Q1 1997 - Mediametrie.

text.p: The number of people who watch television at least once a day in France rose in the first quarter of 1997 compared with the same period last year, French audience measurement body Mediametrie said on Wednesday.
Recent newspaper reports said the number of television viewers in France slumped by a million in the first quarter, but Mediametrie said that was wrong.

"The number of people who watched television on average per day has risen. It is therefore difficult to say that a million television viewers have disappeared, as has unfortunately been asserted," Mediametrie said in a statement.
It said people watched TV for four minutes less in the first quarter compared with 1996's first quarter.
Daily newspapers Le Figaro, Liberation and others said recently that French television had lost a million viewers.
Mediametrie said cold, wet weather in January and unseasonably fine weather in February and March explained a marked variation in the average amount of television viewing earlier this year.

"That without doubt explains the changes in length of watching time seen in France, changes which one also finds at the same period in the countries of Mediterranean and Atlantic Europe," Mediametrie's statement said.
In January there was a rise in both the number of people who watched TV and the amount of television they watched, while in February and March the number of viewers rose, but they watched less TV.

Mediametrie plans to develop an instrument to measure the impact of the weather on television audience numbers and length of TV viewing together with Meteo France, the French weather forecasting body, said Dominique Juchs, head of Mediametrie's television department.
(In 1997 one percent=519,700 people, in 1996 one percent=519,300 people. Figures count adults and children over four.)
